one_line: An agent points a person to the next UI control instead of taking over their account.
what_it_does: Uses a site's interface map and WebMCP to highlight where a user should click, preserving human control and teaching the workflow.
leverage_rationale: Structured interface maps can make guidance precise and shared with the user's live screen; ordinary UI-driving agents would be less reliable and would either guess or take over.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly contrasts pointing at the user's screen with agent control.
Description says the site gives the agent a map of its own interface.
execution_rationale: The concept and intended workflow are coherent, but the packet has no transcript and no inspectable video result; end-to-end completion is not demonstrated in the supplied textual evidence.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive and a public repository exists.
Description specifies a concrete ask-to-highlight workflow.
impact_rationale: Finding settings in complex software is a clear recurring problem for technical and nontechnical users, and the human-in-the-loop approach addresses both immediate friction and learning.
impact_evidence: Examples include Auth0, Jira, and Datadog settings discovery.
Pitch identifies account-control and repeat-learning concerns.
creativity_rationale: Reframes browser agents from autonomous operators into contextual tutors that point at the user's screen, a memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly rejects 'let the agent do it for you' in favor of pointing and waiting.
Learning-through-guidance is central rather than incidental.
usability_note: The proposed ask-and-highlight interaction is simple, with the user retaining control.
red_flags: No video transcript or directly verifiable end-to-end evidence in the packet.
standouts: Strong human-control and learn-the-interface framing.
WebMCP is tied to structured interface state rather than a cosmetic button.
advance_reason: Strong concept and meaningful WebMCP delta; execution should be checked in a later observed stage.

one_line: An agent researches and verifies African travel packages while the traveller controls contact and payment.
what_it_does: Searches, compares, verifies, and shortlists travel packages through structured tools while keeping consequential actions with the traveller.
leverage_rationale: Structured filters, comparison state, verification evidence, and shared shortlist updates materially improve agent research over clicking fragmented travel listings.
leverage_evidence: Description names five WebMCP tools for search, verification, comparison, and shortlist state.
Workflow pauses before agency contact or payment.
execution_rationale: The workflow is unusually well specified and the claimed live interface state is coherent, though the supplied packet lacks directly verified end-to-end demonstration.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported.
Concrete Abuja-to-Umrah budget scenario and explicit no-book/no-pay boundary are given.
impact_rationale: Fragmented packages, inconsistent details, and trust concerns are a real travel-research problem; the product preserves human control at high-consequence boundaries.
impact_evidence: Description identifies WhatsApp, social, and disconnected agency sites as sources of fragmentation.
It surfaces flights, accommodation, visa, transfers, cancellation, and agency verification details.
creativity_rationale: A focused agent-native marketplace for African travel with explicit human approval is a fresh synthesis, even though travel comparison itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Positions the visual marketplace and agent as one shared workflow.
Targets representative African packages rather than a generic itinerary chatbot.
usability_note: The staged research-to-shortlist flow and explicit approval boundary are user-friendly.
red_flags: No transcript and no directly verifiable video outcome in the packet.
standouts: Clear consequential-action boundary.
Specific regional travel problem and structured comparison workflow.
advance_reason: High-value, well-scoped agent research workflow with strong safety framing.

one_line: A release dashboard separates six claims and demands evidence for each boundary.
what_it_does: Tracks source, build, install/runtime, human play, and external release evidence, contradictions, gaps, verification plans, and sanitized handoffs.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP can expose exact live claim IDs, evidence status, and operation context to an agent without letting it overclaim human or external verification; a generic agent can summarize but with more ambiguity.
leverage_evidence: Description emphasizes active release candidate and exact claim IDs as live-page context.
Agent records observations while proof remains pending human review.
execution_rationale: The intentionally incomplete 2-of-6 demo, contradiction handling, quarantine, and privacy scrub form a coherent and unusually disciplined scope.
execution_evidence: Dashboard reports evidence-derived 2/6 coverage.
Features include contradictions, gaps, ordered verification plan, operation log, and sanitized export.
impact_rationale: Small developers and agent-assisted teams have a concrete risk of confusing build completion with release completion; the product directly addresses that evidence gap.
impact_evidence: Six distinct release boundaries are explicitly separated.
Demo intentionally refuses to claim runtime, human-play, or external-release proof without evidence.
creativity_rationale: Treating release readiness as an evidence ledger with honest negative states is an original, thoughtful product framing.
creativity_evidence: The deliberately blocked anonymous demo makes '2 of 6' the product lesson.
Privacy-scrubbed handoff and quarantined observations deepen the concept.
usability_note: The evidence-derived dashboard is clear in principle, though the number of boundaries may add process overhead.
red_flags: No transcript or directly inspectable run evidence supplied.
standouts: Evidence honesty is itself demonstrated by the intentionally incomplete state.
Strong handling of contradictions and privacy.
advance_reason: Strong execution claim and impact with a concrete, differentiated release-integrity workflow.

one_line: Reviewed action packs turn an already-authenticated tab into a bounded WebMCP surface.
what_it_does: Runs declarative, origin-bound action packs in a signed-in browser session with drift checks, bounded output, risk labels, and human approval for writes.
leverage_rationale: The product directly makes otherwise inaccessible authenticated sites agent-addressable through typed, inspectable tools while preserving session permissions and safety constraints; this is substantially beyond generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Runtime registers live WebMCP tools inside the user's signed-in session.
Origin binding, reviewed fingerprints, drift fail-closed, bounded untrusted output, and human authority are core mechanics.
execution_rationale: The architecture, safety boundaries, and adoption model are coherent and detailed; the packet still lacks directly verifiable end-to-end video evidence.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported.
Description specifies declarative manifests, allowlist projection, byte caps, and read/write distinction.
impact_rationale: It targets a broad and real gap: operational sites with authenticated data but no API, while addressing the security risks of giving agents access.
impact_evidence: Examples span Grafana, Cal.com, payer portals, vendor consoles, and admin dashboards.
Frames the login a user already has as the authorization boundary.
creativity_rationale: The user-adopted, reviewed action-pack model inverts the usual vendor-adoption dependency and combines it with strong safety primitives.
creativity_evidence: Adoption occurs one user, one tab, one reviewed pack at a time.
Declarative-never-executable packs and fail-closed drift are distinctive design choices.
usability_note: The safety model is principled, though pack review and origin/fingerprint management may be demanding.
red_flags: Claims are ambitious and need observed validation of pack installation and guarded writes.
standouts: Most direct response to WebMCP's current adoption bottleneck.
Security model is integrated rather than bolted on.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and credible infrastructure thesis; prioritize for observed verification.

one_line: A synthetic lab lets humans inspect, approve, invoke, and verify WebMCP capabilities.
what_it_does: Teaches WebMCP security through deliberately vulnerable tools, comparing presented, declared, authorized, and effective behavior with receipts.
leverage_rationale: The lab's structured tool surface and receipts make authority and actual effect inspectable in a way UI automation alone would not reliably expose.
leverage_evidence: Workflow is public URL to native Site Tool to review, narrow approval, invocation, and verified receipt.
Lessons include read-only tools that mutate and output shaped like instructions.
execution_rationale: The educational test-range workflow is coherent, scoped, and built around concrete vulnerable cases, although run evidence is not directly verifiable here.
execution_evidence: Three surfaces—presented, declared, effective—are explicitly modeled.
Description lists multiple concrete security lessons and a receipt-based completion path.
impact_rationale: As WebMCP adoption grows, developers and users need practical ways to understand authority and confirmation failures; a hands-on lab addresses that learning need.
impact_evidence: Targets both people and AI agents.
Covers schema overreach, vague confirmation, state mutation, and tool-output injection patterns.
creativity_rationale: A deliberately vulnerable interactive range is more memorable and useful than a static security explainer, with a clear three-surface model.
creativity_evidence: Compares promise, declaration, authorization, and actual occurrence.
Requires one exact approved action followed by effect verification.
usability_note: Lesson-based progression and receipts should make abstract security behavior concrete.
red_flags: Synthetic lessons may not represent all production threat models.
standouts: Strong conceptual distinction between declared and effective surfaces.
Security education is interactive rather than merely descriptive.
advance_reason: High-quality educational concept with meaningful WebMCP-specific leverage.

one_line: A shared game engine collects structured human-agent interaction data for learning.
what_it_does: Lets users design and play games with agents through a visible browser interface while capturing observations, actions, and outcomes for ML/RL.
leverage_rationale: Typed observations, legal actions, and shared live state address the fundamental interface mismatch between human play and agent training; generic UI driving would be unreliable for this data collection.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly combines human-visible board interaction with structured agent communication.
Targets partially observable, competitive, sequential human-versus-agent environments.
execution_rationale: The problem framing and platform ambition are coherent, but the packet has no public repository and the supplied evidence does not demonstrate the complete create-play-export loop.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive.
Description defines a gym-style environment and structured training-data goal.
impact_rationale: Human-agent interaction data is a real bottleneck for game-agent research, and a shared environment could support both experimentation and evaluation.
impact_evidence: Connects human-visible interfaces with agent observations and legal-action masks.
Grounds the need in partially observable competitive games and a Kaggle simulation experience.
creativity_rationale: Human-versus-agent game design as a data-collection medium is a genuinely ambitious and memorable use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Combines game authoring, play, sharing, and ML/RL dataset collection.
Treats interface mismatch as the central design opportunity.
usability_note: The concept could be powerful, but authoring and data workflows may be complex and are not demonstrated end-to-end.
red_flags: No public repository and thin completion evidence.
Ambitious platform scope may exceed demonstrated implementation.
standouts: Excellent fit between structured tools and training-data collection.
Novel human-agent interaction arena thesis.
advance_reason: Very strong novelty and leverage justify advancement despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: A shared evidence workspace connects environmental observations to places, dates, hazards, and limitations.
what_it_does: Combines map investigation with official NASA, NOAA, and regional sources, producing cited assessments with confidence, source status, and property-level caveats.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP can translate a natural-language environmental question into shared map choices and structured evidence without losing the human's ability to inspect ambiguity and sources.
leverage_evidence: Agent asks while the page shows the same choices and waits on ambiguous place decisions.
Results include citations, confidence, limitations, and source status in shared state.
execution_rationale: The scope, hazard chains, source catalog, and safety boundaries are unusually explicit and coherent; direct frame verification is unavailable in the packet evidence.
execution_evidence: Seven hazard families and explicit non-merging chains are described.
Examples cover NYC air quality, Las Vegas drought, and Houston Beryl wind observations.
impact_rationale: People need trustworthy, localized environmental evidence after storms and wildfires; official citations and limitations directly address the risk of overinterpreting regional data.
impact_evidence: Use case asks whether smoke or other hazards were recorded near a family or property.
Product explicitly refuses to treat rainfall as wind-damage proof or regional data as a household verdict.
creativity_rationale: The combination of conversational ambiguity handling, map evidence, official-source provenance, and safety limitations is a fresh, deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Broad questions run related hazard chains while named hazards stay focused.
Independent attribution and catalog status are part of the product.
usability_note: The natural-language question flow and visible limitations support informed use, though environmental evidence is inherently complex.
red_flags: External data coverage and credential-dependent sources need observed verification.
standouts: Strong evidence honesty and limitation handling.
Clear shared-state human-agent investigation model.
advance_reason: Excellent impact and evidence-oriented execution claim with strong WebMCP fit.

one_line: A 3D rooftop platformer lets a person and an agent control the same live world.
what_it_does: Provides keyboard, touch, and on-screen controls for a three-stage cat game while WebMCP exposes inspection and timed control to agents.
leverage_rationale: A shared live game state with structured inspection and control is materially different from an agent guessing at a changing canvas; human and agent can alternate control.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says people and agents inspect/control the same live world.
Description names timed WebMCP sequences and manual input taking control back.
execution_rationale: The stated game loop, 3D rendering, controls, stages, hazards, collectibles, and agent console form a coherent product scope; direct verification of frame sheets was unavailable.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported.
Description specifies a three-stage goal and Three.js real-time geometry.
impact_rationale: The primary value is entertainment and experimentation, with legitimate niche value for shared human-agent game play and agent-control research.
impact_evidence: Supports both ordinary play and agent interaction in one world.
Addresses agent difficulty with momentum, moving enemies, gaps, and camera changes.
creativity_rationale: A human-agent co-playable 360-degree rooftop platformer is a memorable and ambitious use of WebMCP beyond business workflows.
creativity_evidence: Three-dimensional world presented as a side-on platformer with orbiting camera.
Manual takeover and timed agent action sequences are part of the interaction model.
usability_note: Multiple control modes and takeover are promising, though agent control of a dynamic platformer is intrinsically demanding.
red_flags: Packet text references screenshots and frame sheets but provides no transcript; full game loop needs observed testing.
standouts: Shared-world control is clearly central, not a bolt-on.
Playful category is pursued with technically ambitious 3D interaction.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-native game concept with credible shared-state interaction.

one_line: Structured tools make a visual map's viewport, camera, places, routes, and pins legible to agents.
what_it_does: Pairs a Leaflet/OpenStreetMap human map with WebMCP operations for exact camera movement, nearby search, distance, routing, and shared pins.
leverage_rationale: Maps are especially resistant to coordinate-free UI automation; exact viewport and meter-based camera tools create reliable shared state unavailable from generic dragging.
leverage_evidence: Description explains why pixel drags are unstable across zoom, screen size, and tile loading.
Tools include viewport inspection, exact location/zoom, nearby places, measurements, routes, and visible shared pins.
execution_rationale: The map problem, tool set, and shared-pin interaction are coherent and appropriately scoped, but the packet lacks direct run evidence beyond the reported live demo.
execution_evidence: Leaflet with real OpenStreetMap tiles is specified.
Central London demo scope and concrete operations are described.
impact_rationale: Reliable map interaction benefits travel, delivery, field work, and emergency response, with a clear pain point for agents operating visual maps.
impact_evidence: Description names ride hailing, food delivery, travel, field work, and emergency response.
Exact camera and viewport state addresses reproducibility and interpretation.
creativity_rationale: The concept turns map gestures into semantic, shared operations and directly attacks a neglected agent-interface problem.
creativity_evidence: Frames maps as moving visual surfaces whose gestures have no stable meaning.
Adds visible shared pins so human and agent see the same result.
usability_note: Keeps familiar human map interaction while adding precise agent operations.
red_flags: No public repository and no directly verifiable end-to-end evidence in the supplied packet.
standouts: Very clear WebMCP delta for a difficult visual domain.
Good balance of normal map UX and structured agent controls.
advance_reason: One of the clearest cases where structured tools materially outperform generic browser automation.

one_line: A private in-tab semantic codex records and recalls tabletop campaign knowledge by meaning.
what_it_does: Lets an agent chronicle NPCs, promises, lies, and plot threads, while humans inspect/edit the same codex and query local embeddings/vector search.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured memory lets the agent write and retrieve semantic campaign state in the same visible tab; generic UI automation would be brittle and would not naturally provide private in-tab retrieval.
leverage_evidence: Human reads and edits the same codex the agent writes.
Embeddings and vector search run in the tab via bundled MiniLM and an in-tab database engine.
execution_rationale: The architecture and core use case are specific and coherent, but the packet does not directly demonstrate long-term write-to-recall completion.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported.
Description defines semantic recording, local embedding, ranked retrieval, and visible editing.
impact_rationale: Tabletop game masters and long-form fiction creators have a real recurring problem of losing continuity across sessions; private semantic recall addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Concrete ferryman/Aldous example shows why keyword search fails.
Privacy requirement is credible because campaigns contain undiscovered secrets.
creativity_rationale: A campaign chronicle that acts as a private, inspectable semantic memory for both keeper and agent is a fresh and well-motivated application.
creativity_evidence: Combines live agent chronicling with weeks-later meaning-based recall.
Local-only embeddings and vector search are architectural commitments serving the concept.
usability_note: Natural-language recall and human editing fit tabletop use, though local model/runtime cost may affect responsiveness.
red_flags: Semantic quality and in-tab model performance require observed testing.
No transcript or directly verifiable run evidence supplied.
standouts: Strong privacy-by-architecture choice.
Clear shared human-agent memory model with a concrete audience.
advance_reason: Distinctive, useful WebMCP-native memory workflow with credible technical rationale.
